summary: Radar for 2026-10-26: no named next-gen drug has a trial result or regulatory step that first went public in the last 48 hours. I checked retatrutide, CagriSema, orforglipron, MariTide, amycretin, survodutide and EloraTZP. Lane C's strict rule isn't met, so today's long-form should be either the best near-fresh follow-up or a Lane P decoder. Top pick: EloraTZP's two Phase 3 trials (AMPLIFY-1 with about 2,115 adults with obesity and no diabetes; AMPLIFY-2 in type 2 diabetes). Both were first posted on ClinicalTrials.gov on Oct 19, and Drug Topics recirculated the story Oct 24. It follows directly from our best video (EloraTZP, 523), has almost no explainer competition, and gives the 20:00 funnel Short a verified target. Mark it lane P (or C-followup), not fresh C. Next: MariTide and amycretin 'What is…?' decoders for no-news days. Then the retatrutide sleep-apnea Phase 3 coverage, still climbing (Medical Xpress and EMJ, Oct 24), as a Short. For Lane A: a NewsNation (Oct 26) 'protein and vitamin D deficiencies' hook refreshes 'Protein on Tirzepatide'. SURMOUNT-4 still anchors 'What happens when you stop'. Thanksgiving is the seasonal evergreen to schedule for mid-November. Instagram body-worry Shorts: bones (Arch Osteoporos systematic review, Oct 23) and a calm, carefully hedged take on the eye-stroke (NAION) pharmacovigilance signal. Research and early news: a semaglutide alcohol-use-disorder RCT is recirculating (Medical Economics, Oct 25), and News-Medical covered GLP-1s and IBD on Oct 26. Rejected: microdosing (Vogue, Yahoo), The Sun's 'injection site trick to boost weight loss', and the research-grade retatrutide sourcing story. Caveat: I couldn't confirm the TRANSCEND-CKD Kidney Week figures from previous snapshots, so I left them out until a primary source is found. The orforglipron EU step (CHMP opinion Oct 15) is 11 days old, and the European Commission's decision is still pending.

candidates.topic: EloraTZP Phase 3 is registered: AMPLIFY-1 (about 2,115 adults with obesity, no diabetes; EloraTZP vs tirzepatide, eloralintide and placebo) and AMPLIFY-2 (about 1,000 adults with obesity/overweight and type 2 diabetes; vs tirzepatide), first posted on ClinicalTrials.gov Oct 19, 2026
candidates.angle: 'EloraTZP Phase 3: What the New Trials Will Test.' A follow-up to our top video. What a co-formulated one-shot amylin plus tirzepatide is, who the trials enrol, what each arm compares, the Phase 2b numbers in context (23.3% vs 14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg at 48 weeks, adults with type 2 diabetes), the most common side effects (nausea and other stomach symptoms), and a dated status: investigational, no approval, 'about 2 years' of participation. No 'beat' frame. Label it lane P (or a C-followup, since it first went public Oct 19 and isn't under 48 h). The 20:00 funnel Short asks 'Why combine amylin with tirzepatide?' and points to the live EloraTZP video.
candidates.predicted_peak: 1–3 weeks (it builds again when first-patient-dosed news lands before year-end)
candidates.why_now: Both Phase 3 registrations went up Oct 19, Drug Topics resurfaced EloraTZP on Oct 24, and Google News is showing 'what is the new Lilly weight loss drug' queries. Our EloraTZP video is 61% of all our GLP-1 long-form views and still growing, and no consumer explainer covers the Phase 3 design yet.

evidence.signal: Phase 3 EloraTZP vs tirzepatide, eloralintide and placebo in obesity without type 2 diabetes, about 2,115 participants
Phase 3 EloraTZP vs tirzepatide in obesity/overweight with type 2 diabetes, about 1,000 participants, about 2 years
Phase 2b: 23.3% vs 14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg at 48 weeks; Phase 3 of a co-formulation planned by end of 2026
Fresh recirculation: 'EloraTZP Shows Greater Weight Loss, A1C Reduction Than Tirzepatide'

How a once-monthly antibody-peptide differs from weekly shots (it activates GLP-1 and blocks GIP), what Phase 2 showed with the population and timeframe named, the common stomach side effects, and a dated status line (investigational, in Phase 3, not approved). No comparison framed as a win.

SURMOUNT-OSA vs TRIUMPH-OSA, separate trials and not head-to-head, the same measure (events per hour) on both sides, the population for each, retatrutide investigational (US filing planned Q1 2027), side effects for each drug. candidates.topic: Protein on tirzepatide: how much and why. Hooked to NewsNation (Oct 26) 'Ozempic users may face protein, vitamin D deficiencies, experts warn' and an ECO 2026 nutrition-monitoring study
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form in the Strength Training mould: 'Protein on Tirzepatide: How Much and Why.' Why appetite drops, what guidelines suggest for protein per meal (general nutrition ranges, no drug dosing), fibre and vitamin D, why a dietitian check-in helps, and easy high-protein options for days with nausea. Encouraging, with no fear framing. End by naming 'Strength Training on Tirzepatide'.

evidence.signal: 'Ozempic users may face protein, vitamin D deficiencies, experts warn'
About 1 in 6 children on GLP-1s were diagnosed with a nutritional deficiency, most often vitamin D. This is a pediatric population; don't generalise it to adults.

What SURMOUNT-4 showed when people switched to placebo vs stayed on it, why weight regain is biology rather than willpower, what helps keep results (protein, strength training, habits), and a clear line: don't stop or change your medicine on your own, talk to your prescriber.

candidates.topic: Can semaglutide reduce heavy drinking? Randomized trial in 108 adults with moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder and obesity (26 weeks, with CBT), resurfacing in Medical Economics (Oct 25), plus BMJ news (Oct 20) on a planned US semaglutide trial in substance use
candidates.angle: Benefits-beyond-weight Short: 'Can GLP-1 medicines curb alcohol cravings?' Heavy-drinking days fell an estimated 13.7 percentage points more than placebo, everyone also got CBT, it's one small trial, and it's not an approved use. How GLP-1 touches the brain's reward system. Point to a clinician for alcohol support. Avoid the 'fights crime' framing.
candidates.why_now: Several outlets (Medical Economics Oct 25, BMJ Oct 20, STAT on off-label telehealth prescribing) are converging. 'GLP-1 and alcohol' is a popular curiosity question, and the RCT evidence is solid if small.

evidence.signal: RCT: 54 vs 54 participants, semaglutide 2.4 mg vs placebo for 26 weeks plus CBT; heavy-drinking days fell 13.7 percentage points more
Planned US trial of semaglutide in substance use with social outcomes

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and 'eye stroke' (NAION): what the pharmacovigilance signal does and doesn't show (Medical Economics, Oct 25: 'Wegovy may pose higher risk of eye stroke than other GLP-1 drugs'), plus the Cureus retinal cohort (Oct 19)

Adverse-event reports can't prove cause or give rates, and the absolute risk is described as very low. Name the warning sign (sudden painless vision loss in one eye) and say to contact a clinician promptly. No scare framing, no brand-first title, no stop advice.
